summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.37% YoY to ₹2,461 million, but PAT after a ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge was ₹233.51 million (+2.35% YoY).
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 22.37% YoY to about ₹2,461 million, with EBITDA up 30.19% to ₹973 million at a 39.54% margin. PAT before exceptional items rose about 71% to ₹391 million, but a ₹209.96 million exceptional charge for restoring securities to two dormant depository clients cut reported PAT to ₹233.51 million. MTF book reached ₹13,318 million (+55% YoY) and distribution AUM ₹94,791 million (+25.82% YoY). Management guided MTF to ₹1,750–1,800 crores and distribution AUM up 40% by year-end FY27.

segments.name: Broking
segments.commentary: Contributed 52% of revenue; broking income ₹1,280 million, up about 7% QoQ, with 51% of it from equity cash, the core focus area.

segments.name: Non-broking (MTF + distribution)
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of revenue; MTF interest income ₹428 million and distribution income ₹275 million. Distribution income dipped QoQ, which management attributed to seasonally lower insurance sales in April–June.

guidance_outlook: MTF book expected at ₹1,750–1,800 crores by end of FY27, from ₹1,330 crores currently.
Distribution AUM targeted to grow about 40%, driven by higher wallet share of existing clients.
Continue to target a near 50:50 broking to non-broking income mix over the medium term.
Long-term revenue growth band of 15–25% (typically 20–25%); PAT growth target of around 30–35% while the mix is not yet 50:50.
Planned Dubai subsidiary to serve UAE-based NRI clients, subject to licences; board has passed a resolution.
Management expects borrowings to rise to lift the debt-equity ratio, which it sees as comfortable at around 2x versus industry 1.5–2x.
capex_capacity: MTF book rose from about ₹1,100 crores at the March 2026 trough to ₹1,330 crores, with growth continuing in Q1.
Management said borrowing is being used to fund working capital and MTF; it expects leverage to rise from 0.81x.
Credit rating upgraded: short-term bank facilities to A1+, long-term to A+.
Dubai subsidiary planned for NRI servicing; a GIFT City subsidiary already exists and is active for NRI business.
demand_pricing: Cash market turnover rose about 13% QoQ, while derivatives activity moderated after SEBI measures (upfront option premium, expiry-day margins, higher contract sizes, weekly expiry rationalisation).
RBI revised capital market exposure framework effective 1 July 2026 is expected to raise bank working-capital costs for broking intermediaries.
MTF yield about 14%; management said spreads depend on market liquidity and borrowing costs, which are currently higher.
Demat accounts reached 23 crore in June; SIP additions about 66 lakh in June versus 53 lakh in March; 42 companies filed draft offer documents with SEBI in the quarter.

Distribution revenue in April–June fell QoQ because insurance sales are concentrated in January–March; mutual fund and other AUM grew QoQ and the company recorded its highest net collections in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MTF interest income flat despite about 21% book growth, and is MTF pricing falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Average MTF book was flat QoQ because it fell to about ₹1,100 crores in March after a mid-cap sell-off of about 15%, then recovered to ₹1,330 crores by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF risk management approach?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF is funded only against cash-market securities chosen from a restricted list, with no F&O allocation, per-customer and per-scrip limits, and a book mostly below ₹1 crore per client. Management said there have been no delinquencies since 2017.

qa_highlights.question: What was the fraud, and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Two dormant depository clients lost securities through fraudulent off-market transfers noticed about a year later. The company replenished the securities, filed an FIR with EOW (assets frozen), lodged an insurance claim, appointed EY for forensic audit and hired an external consultant. Recoveries will be booked only when reasonably certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth guidance given the 22% Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for 20–25% growth, within a 15–25% range, with PAT growth of 30–35%, until the 50:50 broking and non-broking mix is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-broking decline QoQ and how will this be avoided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is seasonal, with insurance sales concentrated in January–March; the April–June fall was driven by insurance, while other products grew. Trail revenue was also hit by the March market fall.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt-equity elevated and will leverage increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity fell after the IPO equity infusion; management intends to borrow more to fund MTF and working capital, saying 1.5–2x is comfortable for the industry, versus 0.81x now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF yield and the sustainability of spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF yield is about 14%. Management said spreads depend on liquidity, with borrowing costs currently higher, and that higher costs can be passed to clients.

risks_watch: ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge; recovery depends on insurance claim settlement and frozen assets, with timing uncertain. External forensic audit still in progress.
RBI capital market exposure framework from 1 July 2026 may raise bank borrowing costs and working-capital needs for brokers.
MTF book (₹13,318 million) is sensitive to market sell-offs, as the March 2026 trough showed; leverage is planned to rise from 0.81x.
Derivatives activity is moderating under SEBI curbs, and distribution revenue is seasonal.
Dubai subsidiary licensing and GIFT City international offering are still early-stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, the MTF book and regulatory fit, but cautious on near-term market volatility. Management was open on the fraud and its controls, though it gave no quantified recovery estimate, and it was vague on customer acquisition cost. Its answer on the 15–25% growth band was less precise than its 20–25% target.
key_quotes: So whatever FII outflow we have seen, we have already, experienced in in later days, in initial days of July first week, I think that have mellowed down to a great extent and over a period of time I think this may become positive.
And again, if you really see our book position, our large portion of book position is below ₹1 crores.
So, it's a positive thing, in the sense that we are not crossing the boundaries and we are not over-leveraging that.

growth.why: Management guides MTF book to ₹1,750–1,800 crore and distribution AUM up ~40% by FY27 end, backed by a 55% YoY MTF rise and wallet-share gains, but no new capacity or order-book figures are given; long-term revenue growth guided at a 15–20% minimum (PAT 30–35%).
